Sinuses.Comments: 0.6 mm reformats Cor and Sag. Bone plus and Soft

Orbits.Comments: 0.6mm reformats Cor and Sag. Bone plus and Soft

Orbital cellulitis/Complications of mast.Comments: 0.6mm reformats Cor and Sag. Bone plus and Soft

Pituitary.Comments: 0.6mm reformats Cor and Sag. Bone plus and Soft

IAMS.Parameters: Helical Head pre Helical IAMs post
IAMS.Comments: 0.6mm reformats Cor and Sag. Bone plus and Soft

Petrous.Comments: 0.6mm reformats Cor and Sag. Bone plus and Soft

Neck Oncology.Parameters: 100s delay Sup orbital margin to lung apices
Neck Oncology.Comments: 3mm Axial, Sag and Cor reformats. Bone reformats. Arms by side. Quiet respiration.

Neck Thyroid Multi Nodular Goitre.Comments: 3mm Axial, Sag and Cor reformats. Bone reformats. Arms by side. Quiet respiration

4D Neck.Comments: 3mm Axial, Sag and Cor reformats. Bone reformats. Arms by side. Quiet respiration

Neck infection.Comments: 3mm Axial, Sag and Cor reformats. Bone reformats. Arms by side. Quiet respiration

HR Thorax.Parameters: Inspiration (Supine), If requested Inspiration (Prone) carina to lung bases

Breast Cancer.Parameters: PV CAP 70s delay Including supraclavicular fossa

Oesophagus & Gastric, Neuroendocrine.Prep: 1 litre water 0.5 hours before scan. 1 glass water immediately before the scan. NBM 6 hours prior.

Pancreatic Cancer.Prep: 500ml water 1.5 hours before scan. 2 glasses water immediately before the scan.

TCC upper track Surveillance.Prep: 500ml water 1.5 hours before scan. 1 glass of water immediately before.

KUB Calculus.Parameters: Prone. Lowish dose + Dual energy if calculus seen.

Melanoma.Prep: 1st Visit: Omni 25ml in 500ml water 2 hours before scan. Omni 25ml in 500ml water 1 hour before scan. Water only for follow up.

Gynae cancer.Prep: Omni 25ml in 500ml water 2 hours before scan. Omni 25ml in 500ml water 1 hour before scan.

Carotids.Parameters: Arterial Aortic arch to skull base

Dissection.Parameters: Pre Thorax. Arterial CAP from C6 to symph.

Pulmonary Angio.Parameters: Top of aortic arch to base of heart. Unless specified by radiologist.

Brain tumours - primary.protocol: Pre-contrast CT head, post-contrast if abnormal.

Brain tumours - metastatic.protocol: Post-contrast CT head if specifically requested.

Post brain tumour resection.protocol: Initial CT as pre- and post-contrast CT head to differentiate post-op haemorrhage from residual tumour.

Head and neck (squamous cell carcinoma).protocol: Dual-phase CT neck (arterial and venous) and chest.

Mesothelioma or suspected pleural diseas.protocol: CT high chest and abdomen + IV.

Oesophageal cancer.protocol: CT chest and abdomen + IV + water.

Suspected primary hepatic lesion(s).protocol: i) Cirrhosis and suspected HCC or post-TACE: CT abdomen with Iomeron-400, 4-phase (pre, arterial 35s, venous 70s, equilibrium 180s). Include CT chest if requested or in primary liver malignancy. ii) Suspected benign lesion (haemangioma, adenoma, FNH) and HCC not suspected: MRI first line unless contraindicated/unavailable, in which case CT abdomen arterial + venous + equilibrium.

Suspected hepatic metastases.protocol: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis + IV. Consider arterial phase CT abdomen for hypervascular metastases (thyroid, RCC, neuroendocrine, melanoma, choriocarcinoma).

Pancreatic cancer and cholangiocarcinoma.protocol: Ultrasound is primary for biliary obstruction. CT if pancreatic neoplasm suspected: CT chest, pre-contrast and arterial phase (40s) abdomen, venous phase abdomen and pelvis + water. Pre-contrast to look for stone disease.

Colorectal cancer.protocol: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis + IV.

Anal canal cancer.protocol: CT chest, abdomen, pelvis and groins + IV.

Renal malignancy.protocol: Triple-phase CT renal (pre, 30s and 100s) + CT chest. Add pelvis if local symptoms (e.g. bone pain).

Ureter/upper urothelial tumour.protocol: Haematuria with pain: CT KUB + CT urogram + water. Painless haematuria: CT urogram + water.

Bladder tumour – staging and follow up.protocol: CT urogram (split-dose IV contrast) + water. Add CT chest if requested.

Prostate (staging & follow up).protocol: CT abdomen & pelvis + IV + water. Add CT chest if requested.

Testicular tumour for staging and follow.protocol: CT chest, abdomen & pelvis + IV. Pelvis can be omitted on follow-up if inguinal orchidectomy.

Adrenal nodule assessment.protocol: Pre-contrast CT abdomen + review. If homogeneous and <10 HU: stop. If non-homogeneous or >10 HU: + IV and image at 1 min and 15 min.

Adrenocortical cancer.protocol: Pre-contrast CT abdomen + CT chest and abdomen (65s).

Cervical cancer.indication: Cervical cancer (CT only if unable to have MRI)

Vulval and vaginal cancer.indication: Vulval / vaginal cancer (CT only if unable to have MRI)

Liver - Lesion characterization.notes: If you also want to scan the whole abdomen, do it during the 1st or 2nd scan.

Liver - Metastases.notes: Use this protocol when you are sure that you are dealing with hypovascular metastases.

Pancreas - Carcinoma / Pancreatitis.optional: Upper Abdomen w/o contrast to look for calcifications indicating chronic pancreatitis.

Abdomen ileus.scan_range: Scan from top diaphragm to just below the symphysis.
Abdomen ileus.optional: Optional: repeat scan at 70 sec p.i.

steps.note: if lesion <10HU you can stop. If >10HU continue

Abdomen Trauma - Blunt.notes: Long delay to get some filling of urinary collecting system.

Abdomen Trauma - Penetrating injury.notes: Like Blunt Trauma, but if there is no reason for emergency surgery, continue with:

steps.step: Repeat lower abdomen after installation of contrast through catheter + 40 cm.
Stop contrast inflow when flow stops, or after 350 cc, or when patient no longer tolerates.

Abdomen Anastomosis leakage.prep: Insert a cannula for 800 cc rectal contrast (50 cc in 750 cc water), but do not give the rectal contrast until everything is ready for scanning.
Abdomen Anastomosis leakage.notes: Right after delivery of rectal contrast, inject IV contrast. Tell patient to hold rectal contrast in (about 2 minutes). After the scan, enter the room quickly and let the rectal contrast out.

Kidney.indication: Haematuria / possible urothelial cancer or RCC
Kidney.prep: Drink 1 L water during 1/2 hour before start of examination.

steps.step: Wait 10 minutes to fill the urinary excretion system.
Place ROI in right atrium or pulmonary trunk.
Fast scanner: scan from top to bottom.
Slow scanner: scan caudally to cranially (fewer breathing artefacts in lower lobes where most emboli are).
Start 5 cm below top of diaphragm to scan entire lower lobes.
Explain to patient to breathe in normally, not forcefully (forceful breath draws non-contrast blood from IVC into pulmonary circulation).

CT GI Bleed / GI Haemorrhage.Prep: None. No oral contrast — masks active luminal bleeding.
CT GI Bleed / GI Haemorrhage.Parameters: CT AP triphasic — non-contrast + arterial 35 s + PV 70 s
CT GI Bleed / GI Haemorrhage.Comments: Localisation of active GI bleeding (angiodysplasia, diverticular, tumour, varices)

CT Brain — Dementia Assessment.Parameters: Plain CT brain + coronal reformats through medial temporal lobes
CT Brain — Dementia Assessment.Comments: Hippocampal atrophy (Scheltens score). Exclude structural cause (SOL, NPH, chronic SDH, vascular burden). MRI first line when available.

CT Anastomosis Leak / Post-Op Bowel.Prep: Rectal water-soluble contrast 50 mL in 750 mL water via rectal tube
CT Anastomosis Leak / Post-Op Bowel.Parameters: Rectal contrast instilled immediately before scanning. CT AP.
CT Anastomosis Leak / Post-Op Bowel.Comments: Detection of anastomotic leak, post-op collection, or abscess following bowel / colorectal surgery

CT Liver 4-Phase (HCC / Post-TACE).Parameters: 4-phase: plain + arterial 35 s + portal venous 70 s + equilibrium 180 s. Include CT chest if requested.
CT Liver 4-Phase (HCC / Post-TACE).Comments: HCC characterisation, post-TACE evaluation, LI-RADS reporting. Arterial hyperenhancement + washout.

CT Internal Auditory Meati (IAMs).Contrast: 50 mL hand inject if mass suspected
CT Internal Auditory Meati (IAMs).Parameters: Helical head pre-contrast + helical high-resolution IAMs
CT Internal Auditory Meati (IAMs).Comments: High-resolution CT temporal bones and IAMs for bony detail (cholesteatoma, otosclerosis, trauma, canal dehiscence). MRI first line for vestibular schwannoma.

CT Subclavian Angiography.Parameters: CTA hyoid to below elbow affected side
CT Subclavian Angiography.Comments: Subclavian artery + upper limb vasculature — stenosis, occlusion, dissection, aneurysm, thoracic outlet compression

CT Renal Cyst Characterisation.Parameters: Pre-contrast through renal area + post-contrast portal venous AP. Measure HU pre vs post.
CT Renal Cyst Characterisation.Comments: Bosniak classification of indeterminate renal lesions. Enhancement > 20 HU increase = solid/enhancing.

CT Pulmonary Angiography — Pregnancy.Parameters: CTPA lung coverage only. No bismuth shield.
CT Pulmonary Angiography — Pregnancy.Comments: PE in pregnancy when V/Q unavailable or non-diagnostic. Per NICE NG158. Foetal dose < 0.1 mGy.

CT Gastric (Stomach) Cancer.Prep: 1 litre water 0.5 hours before scan. 1 glass water immediately before.

CT Pancreas Cancer Follow-up.Parameters: PV abdomen for chemo response. Arterial + PV if operable.
CT Pancreas Cancer Follow-up.Comments: Follow-up assessment. Arterial phase abdomen if surgical candidate.

CT Adrenal Washout (Nodule Characterisat.Parameters: Pre-contrast adrenal area. If homogeneous and < 10 HU — stop. If non-homogeneous or > 10 HU — IV at 1 min and 15 min delay.
CT Adrenal Washout (Nodule Characterisat.Comments: Adrenal washout calculation. Absolute washout > 60% or relative > 40% = adenoma.

CT Adrenocortical Carcinoma.Parameters: Pre-contrast CT abdomen + CT chest and abdomen at 65 s

CT Hepatic Metastases (Hypervascular).Parameters: PV CAP. Consider arterial phase CT abdomen for hypervascular metastases (thyroid, RCC, neuroendocrine, melanoma, choriocarcinoma).

CT Chest Routine.Prep: None for routine. Remove chest metal artefacts. Arms above head.
CT Chest Routine.Contrast: 70–100 mL @ 2.5–3 mL/s. Bolus tracking in descending aorta, trigger 100 HU + 8 s, or fixed delay 40 s.
CT Chest Routine.Parameters: Single phase portal venous CT chest (lung apices to adrenals). Inspiration breath-hold. Reconstruct lung, mediastinal, and bone windows.
CT Chest Routine.Comments: Standard enhanced chest for infection, malignancy workup, metastatic screening. Unenhanced chest (HRCT or low-dose) for ILD, follow-up nodules. RCR iRefer.

CT Abdomen Pelvis – Triphasic (Liver).Contrast: 120–150 mL iodinated contrast (350–370 mg I/mL) @ 5 mL/s via 18 G.
CT Abdomen Pelvis – Triphasic (Liver).Parameters: Triple phase CT AP: 1) Late arterial (35–40 s p.i. or +15 s after bolus trigger) — liver only. 2) Portal venous (70–75 s p.i.) — full AP coverage. 3) Delayed (180 s p.i.) — liver only if lesion needing washout assessment.
CT Abdomen Pelvis – Triphasic (Liver).Comments: HCC characterisation, hypervascular metastases (NET, RCC, thyroid, melanoma), liver lesion characterisation. LI-RADS diagnostic criteria: APHE + washout + capsule = LR-5.

CT HRCT Chest.Prep: Explain breath-hold technique to patient. No contrast.
CT HRCT Chest.Parameters: Volumetric inspiratory CT chest 1–1.5 mm slices + sharp lung reconstruction. Expiratory sequence (supine) — targeted 10 mm gap slices for air-trapping. Optional prone inspiratory scans if dependent atelectasis obscures posterobasal segments.
CT HRCT Chest.Comments: ILD workup (UIP/NSIP, HP, sarcoid), bronchiectasis, small airways disease. Fleischner Society CT standards. Dose-optimise with tube current modulation.

CT Carotid Angiography.Prep: 18 G cannula (ideally right antecubital to reduce streak artefact from left brachiocephalic vein).
CT Carotid Angiography.Parameters: Arterial phase aortic arch to vertex. Bolus tracking in ascending aorta trigger 100 HU + 6 s diagnostic delay. Coverage includes circle of Willis.
CT Carotid Angiography.Comments: Carotid stenosis (NASCET method), dissection, pre-CEA/CAS planning, vertebrobasilar insufficiency. Often combined with NCCT brain in acute stroke pathway.

CT Stroke Protocol (NCCT + CTA ± CTP).Prep: 18 G cannula right antecubital. Do NOT delay for eGFR in acute stroke.
CT Stroke Protocol (NCCT + CTA ± CTP).Contrast: CTA: 50–80 mL @ 4–5 mL/s. CTP: 40 mL @ 5 mL/s.
CT Stroke Protocol (NCCT + CTA ± CTP).Parameters: 1) NCCT brain (ASPECTS scoring, exclude haemorrhage). 2) CTA arch to vertex (single bolus tracked in ascending aorta). 3) CTP optional — cine mode through basal ganglia/whole brain for Tmax, CBF, CBV, MTT maps. Mismatch determines penumbra.
CT Stroke Protocol (NCCT + CTA ± CTP).Comments: NICE NG128. Target door-to-CT <20 min. LVO on CTA activates thrombectomy pathway (up to 24 h with perfusion mismatch per DAWN/DEFUSE-3). CTP for late window selection.

CT Temporal Bone.Contrast: None (rarely given — only if mass suspected and MRI unavailable).
CT Temporal Bone.Parameters: Helical volumetric petrous temporal bones. 0.5–0.625 mm thin slices. Bone algorithm (sharp kernel). Reconstruct 0.6 mm axial + coronal + Pöschl (long axis SSC) + Stenvers (short axis SSC) views.
CT Temporal Bone.Comments: Cholesteatoma, otosclerosis, superior semicircular canal dehiscence, trauma (ossicular disruption, petrous fracture classification). MRI preferred for vestibular schwannoma and inflammatory disease.

CT CAP (Staging).Prep: 500–1000 mL water 1 hour before. Cannula 18 G.
CT CAP (Staging).Contrast: 100–120 mL @ 3 mL/s. Bolus tracking or fixed 70 s delay.
CT CAP (Staging).Parameters: Single portal venous phase chest-abdomen-pelvis. Lung apices to pubic symphysis. Arms above head. Axial 1–3 mm + coronal/sagittal reformats + lung recon.
CT CAP (Staging).Comments: Oncology staging workhorse (lung, breast, colorectal, melanoma, lymphoma, CUP). Single acquisition spanning all 3 body regions in PV phase. Add arterial phase only for HCC, NET, hypervascular mets.

CT Abdomen and Pelvis -Plain.Prep: No oral contrast. Consider positive oral contrast only if specifically requested (e.g. known perforation).
CT Abdomen and Pelvis -Plain.Parameters: Single non-contrast CT AP. Diaphragm to symphysis. Standard and soft tissue reconstructions.
CT Abdomen and Pelvis -Plain.Comments: Renal / ureteric colic (stones), follow-up post-procedure, contrast-contraindicated cases. NICE NG118: low-dose CTKUB first line for suspected stones.

CT Abdomen and Pelvis - Portal Venous Ph.Prep: 500–1000 mL water orally 60 min before (neutral gastric/proximal bowel distension). Water glass at table.
CT Abdomen and Pelvis - Portal Venous Ph.Contrast: 100 mL (body-weight adjusted: 75 kg → 100 mL, 75–90 kg → 120 mL, >90 kg → 150 mL) iopamidol-370 or iohexol-350 @ 3 mL/s. Bolus tracking in aorta trigger 150 HU + 60 s diagnostic delay, or fixed 70 s.
CT Abdomen and Pelvis - Portal Venous Ph.Parameters: Single portal venous phase AP, diaphragm to pubic symphysis. Arms above head. Axial 1–3 mm, coronal + sagittal reformats.
CT Abdomen and Pelvis - Portal Venous Ph.Comments: Workhorse CT AP protocol. Infection, inflammation, malignancy workup. Do not use oral iodinated contrast unless suspected perforation.

CT Liver Triphasic.Contrast: 120–150 mL iodinated contrast 350–400 mg I/mL @ 5 mL/s via 18 G.
CT Liver Triphasic.Parameters: Liver only, three phases: 1) late arterial 35–40 s p.i. 2) portal venous 70 s p.i. 3) delayed 180 s p.i. Coverage: dome of diaphragm to iliac crest.
CT Liver Triphasic.Comments: Liver lesion characterisation when 4-phase (plain + 3 post-contrast) not required. Core clinical scenarios: known/suspected HCC, haemangioma atypical, FNH.

CT Pancreas Protocol.Prep: NBM 4 h pre-scan. 500 mL water 1 h before + 2 glasses water at the table (gastric/duodenal distension).
CT Pancreas Protocol.Contrast: 120–150 mL iodinated contrast 370 mg I/mL @ 5 mL/s.
CT Pancreas Protocol.Parameters: Multiphase: 1) Non-contrast (optional — for calcifications of chronic pancreatitis). 2) Late arterial / pancreatic parenchymal phase 40 s p.i. — pancreas only, thin slice 1 mm. 3) Portal venous 70 s p.i. — full AP. Reconstruct multiplanar and curved MPRs along pancreatic duct.
CT Pancreas Protocol.Comments: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma staging (resectability), cystic pancreatic lesions, IPMN. Pancreatic phase optimal for lesion-parenchyma contrast. Assess arterial invasion (SMA, coeliac, hepatic) and venous involvement (PV, SMV).

CT Urogram.Prep: 500 mL water 1 h before. Void bladder 30 min before. Consider IV furosemide 10 mg if renal function permits to distend collecting system.
CT Urogram.Contrast: Split-bolus: 30 mL @ 2 mL/s (delayed excretory bolus) wait 8 min, then 70 mL @ 3 mL/s. OR single-bolus triphasic 100 mL.
CT Urogram.Parameters: Three phases: 1) Unenhanced KUB (stones). 2) Nephrographic phase 90 s (cortex/medulla equilibration — RCC detection). 3) Excretory/pyelographic phase 7–10 min (opacified collecting system and ureters).
CT Urogram.Comments: Haematuria workup — TCC, RCC, stones. NICE NG12. Split-bolus technique reduces dose by combining nephrographic + excretory into one acquisition.

CT Whole Body Trauma.Prep: None — follow ATLS primary survey. Remove radiopaque artefacts if safe. 18 G+ cannula.
CT Whole Body Trauma.Contrast: 100–150 mL @ 4–5 mL/s. Split-bolus or multi-phase depending on centre protocol.
CT Whole Body Trauma.Parameters: 1) Non-contrast CT head and cervical spine. 2) Arterial phase neck/chest (30 s) + portal venous abdomen/pelvis (70 s) — OR split-bolus single acquisition with arterial + PV mix. Arms below or sleeved.
CT Whole Body Trauma.Comments: RCR Standards for Providing a 24-Hour CT Service 2024: WBCT if GCS <14, SBP <90, RR <10 or >29, SaO2 <93%, high-energy mechanism. Report top-to-toe systematically.

CT Aortic Angiography.Prep: Cannula 18 G antecubital (ideally right). ECG gating if thoracic aorta / aortic root / Type A dissection.
CT Aortic Angiography.Contrast: 100 mL iodinated contrast 370 mg I/mL @ 4–5 mL/s + 30 mL saline chase.
CT Aortic Angiography.Parameters: Non-contrast thorax + arterial CTA C6 to femoral heads. Bolus tracking in descending aorta trigger 120 HU + 5 s.
CT Aortic Angiography.Comments: Acute aortic syndrome (dissection, IMH, PAU), ruptured AAA, pre/post TEVAR/EVAR. Non-contrast scan detects IMH. ECG gating for aortic root and Type A dissection.

CT Facial Bones (Volume).Prep: None. Remove dentures and facial metal artefacts if safe.
CT Facial Bones (Volume).Parameters: Helical volumetric CT frontal sinus to mandible. 0.6–1 mm slices. Bone and soft tissue algorithms. Axial + coronal + sagittal + 3D surface rendering.
CT Facial Bones (Volume).Comments: Facial trauma (Le Fort classification, NOE complex, orbital floor, zygomaticomaxillary, mandibular fractures), pre-maxillofacial surgical planning, facial bone tumour.

CT Thoracic Spine.Contrast: None for routine. IV if tumour or infection.
CT Thoracic Spine.Parameters: Helical C7 to L1. 0.6–1 mm slices. Bone + soft tissue. Multiplanar reformats.
CT Thoracic Spine.Comments: Trauma, vertebral fracture, degenerative disease, metastatic workup. Often done as part of whole-body trauma CT.

CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis non-staging (-C/.Contrast: 100 mL @ 3 mL/s. Optional non-contrast pass if baseline HU required.
CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis non-staging (-C/.Parameters: Pre-contrast CAP (if indicated) + portal venous CAP (70 s). Lung apices to symphysis.
CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis non-staging (-C/.Comments: General oncological or inflammatory workup where staging phase not required. Non-contrast pre-scan only if truly needed (dose penalty).

CT Abdomen & Pelvis – -Non-Staging (2 Ph.Parameters: Pre-contrast through liver + portal venous phase full AP. 70 s delay.
CT Abdomen & Pelvis – -Non-Staging (2 Ph.Comments: When baseline HU measurement needed (e.g. adrenal washout baseline, characterising indeterminate focal liver lesion without full triphasic).

CT Abdomen & Pelvis – Staging (3 Phase).Parameters: Pre-contrast liver + late arterial (35 s) liver + portal venous (70 s) full AP. Arms above head.
CT Abdomen & Pelvis – Staging (3 Phase).Comments: Hepatic/pancreatic malignancy staging where arterial phase needed for arterial enhancement pattern or vascular mapping. Add delayed 180 s phase if fibrotic lesion suspected (cholangiocarcinoma).

CT Renal Injury + CT Cystogram.Prep: 18 G cannula. Catheterise bladder for cystogram component (if not already in-situ).
CT Renal Injury + CT Cystogram.Contrast: IV: 100–120 mL @ 3–5 mL/s. Bladder: 250–350 mL dilute contrast (30 mL in 500 mL saline) instilled by gravity via catheter.
CT Renal Injury + CT Cystogram.Parameters: Renal: arterial 25 s + portal venous 70 s + excretory/delayed 5–10 min (for collecting system injury and urinoma). Cystogram: retrograde bladder distension with dilute contrast, then axial/coronal/sagittal acquisition.
CT Renal Injury + CT Cystogram.Comments: Blunt/penetrating renal trauma (AAST grading), suspected bladder rupture (intra- vs extraperitoneal). Delayed phase essential to detect urine leak. Cystogram differentiates bladder injury location.

CT Abdominal ileus/SBO.Prep: No oral contrast (preserves bowel-wall enhancement and fluid contrast).
CT Abdominal ileus/SBO.Parameters: Single portal venous phase CT AP, diaphragm to symphysis. Reconstruct axial + coronal + sagittal. Thin slices 1 mm.
CT Abdominal ileus/SBO.Comments: Small bowel obstruction workup: identify transition point, closed-loop, strangulation (reduced/absent wall enhancement, congestion of mesentery, pneumatosis, portal venous gas). Differentiate mechanical SBO from ileus.

CT Mesenteric CTA.Prep: 18 G cannula. Do NOT give oral contrast (obscures bowel wall enhancement).
CT Mesenteric CTA.Parameters: Triphasic: 1) Non-contrast (optional, for hyperdense blood/intramural haemorrhage). 2) Arterial 25–30 s (bolus tracking at coeliac axis). 3) Portal venous 70 s. Diaphragm to symphysis.
CT Mesenteric CTA.Comments: Acute mesenteric ischaemia (embolic, thrombotic, NOMI, venous), mesenteric arterial stenosis, pre-bypass planning. Assess coeliac, SMA, IMA origins. Look for bowel wall pneumatosis, portal venous gas, bowel wall enhancement changes.

CT Abdominal Aorta CTA.Parameters: Arterial phase diaphragm to common femoral arteries. Bolus tracking in infrarenal aorta trigger 150 HU + 5 s. Optional delayed phase if endoleak suspected post-EVAR.
CT Abdominal Aorta CTA.Comments: AAA surveillance, pre/post EVAR planning, endoleak detection. Measure AP and transverse diameters perpendicular to aortic long axis.

CT Renal CTA (Volume).Parameters: Arterial phase renal arteries (bolus tracking in aorta just above coeliac, trigger 150 HU + 5 s). Coverage diaphragm to iliac crests. Optional nephrographic phase for parenchyma and venous phase for renal vein.
CT Renal CTA (Volume).Comments: Renal artery stenosis (FMD, atheromatous), living donor assessment (anatomy of renal arteries/veins), RCC vascular mapping, post-transplant.

CT Lumbar Spine.Contrast: None for routine. IV if tumour, infection, or post-op.
CT Lumbar Spine.Parameters: Helical T12 to S1. 0.6–1 mm slices. Bone + soft tissue kernels. Sagittal and coronal reformats.
CT Lumbar Spine.Comments: Trauma, canal stenosis (when MRI contraindicated), spondylolysis, fracture. MRI preferred for disc/nerve root assessment.

CT Sacrum / Coccyx.Contrast: None for trauma. IV if tumour/infection.
CT Sacrum / Coccyx.Parameters: Helical L5 to coccyx tip. 0.6 mm slices. Bone + soft tissue. Sagittal and coronal reformats. Include oblique reformats along sacral planes.
CT Sacrum / Coccyx.Comments: Sacral insufficiency fracture, sacrococcygeal trauma, chordoma, sacroiliitis (limited — MRI preferred), pilonidal disease complications.

CT Bony Pelvis.Prep: None. Remove metal from pelvic region if safe.
CT Bony Pelvis.Contrast: None for routine skeletal. IV for tumour/infection.
CT Bony Pelvis.Parameters: Helical iliac crests to ischial tuberosities. 0.6–1 mm slices. Bone algorithm primary. Coronal, sagittal, and 3D reformats (Young–Burgess or Tile classification for fractures).
CT Bony Pelvis.Comments: Pelvic ring injury (trauma), acetabular fractures, sacral fractures, pre-op planning for arthroplasty.

CT Cervical Spine.Prep: None. Immobilise if trauma. Arms down.
CT Cervical Spine.Contrast: None for routine trauma. IV contrast if neoplastic/infectious.
CT Cervical Spine.Parameters: Helical volumetric skull base to T4. 0.6–1 mm thin slices. Bone + soft tissue algorithms. Sagittal and coronal reformats.
CT Cervical Spine.Comments: Trauma (NEXUS/Canadian C-spine rules), fracture detection, pre-op planning, metastatic assessment. Follow NICE NG41 for trauma imaging criteria.

CT Neck/Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis Non-Staging.Parameters: Single portal venous phase skull base/hyoid to symphysis. Arms above head. Neck included in single bolus acquisition.
CT Neck/Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis Non-Staging.Comments: General infection/inflammation/lymphoma surveillance, unknown primary workup with neck cover. Non-staging = single phase.

CT Neck/Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis Staging (2.Prep: 500 mL water 1 h before. NBM 4 h for gastric/oesophageal cases.
CT Neck/Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis Staging (2.Parameters: Two phases: 1) Neck/head arterial 40–50 s (SCC mucosal hyperaemia). 2) Portal venous CAP 70 s. Full coverage skull base to symphysis.
CT Neck/Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis Staging (2.Comments: Head and neck SCC staging, nasopharyngeal/oropharyngeal carcinoma, unknown primary with cervical lymphadenopathy. Arterial phase through neck essential.

CT Lower Extremities (Joints or Bone).Contrast: None for routine. IV for tumour/infection.
CT Lower Extremities (Joints or Bone).Parameters: Helical volumetric through joint or bone of interest. 0.6–1 mm slices. Bone + soft tissue reconstructions. Multiplanar and 3D reformats as needed.
CT Lower Extremities (Joints or Bone).Comments: Complex intra-articular fracture (tibial plateau, pilon, calcaneus), pre-operative planning, bone tumour characterisation, stress fractures, infection assessment.

CT Upper Extremities (Joints or Bone).Prep: None. Ideally position arm above head (superman) to reduce streak artefact.
CT Upper Extremities (Joints or Bone).Contrast: None for routine. IV for tumour/infection.
CT Upper Extremities (Joints or Bone).Parameters: Helical volumetric through joint/bone. 0.6–1 mm slices. Bone + soft tissue kernels. Multiplanar and 3D reformats.
CT Upper Extremities (Joints or Bone).Comments: Complex fractures (scaphoid, wrist, elbow, proximal humerus), bone tumour assessment, pre-operative planning.

CT 4D Parathyroid (Four-Phase).Contrast: 100 mL iodinated contrast 370 mg I/mL @ 3–4 mL/s.
CT 4D Parathyroid (Four-Phase).Parameters: Four phases through neck (skull base to aortic arch): 1) Non-contrast. 2) Arterial 25 s. 3) Early venous 80 s. 4) Delayed 180 s. Thin 1 mm slices + MPR.
CT 4D Parathyroid (Four-Phase).Comments: Primary hyperparathyroidism — localise adenoma when Tc-99m-sestamibi scintigraphy negative/equivocal. Adenoma classic pattern: low on NC, hyperenhancing on arterial, rapid washout on delayed. Include mediastinum for ectopic adenoma.
